title: Samsung Biologics Launches $1.8 Billion Bid for PolyPeptide, Expanding Into GLP-1 Drug Manufacturing
excerpt: South Korea's largest biopharma CDMO will acquire Swiss peptide specialist PolyPeptide in an all-cash deal that expands its manufacturing network across the US, Europe, and India.
body:
• Samsung Biologics will acquire PolyPeptide for CHF 1.46 billion ($1.81 billion) in an all-cash tender offer at CHF 44.31 per share
  • The deal expands Samsung Biologics into peptide-based therapeutics, including fast-growing GLP-1 obesity and diabetes treatments
  • PolyPeptide operates manufacturing sites across Sweden, Belgium, France, the US, and India, giving Samsung global reach
  • PolyPeptide's board unanimously recommends the offer; its largest shareholder, holding 55.65%, has committed to tender all shares

Korea's Biggest Pharma Deal

Samsung Biologics, South Korea's leading contract development and manufacturing organisation, announced an all-cash public tender offer to acquire 100% of PolyPeptide Group AG, a Swiss company specialising in peptide-based active pharmaceutical ingredients. The offer values PolyPeptide at approximately CHF 1.46 billion ($1.81 billion).

At CHF 44.31 per share, the bid represents a 40% premium to PolyPeptide's undisturbed share price on April 10, before market rumours of a potential acquisition emerged. It is approximately 6.1% above the stock's most recent closing price. The tender offer is expected to launch by the end of August 2026, with completion targeted for year-end.

The GLP-1 Imperative

The acquisition is driven by the explosive growth of peptide-based therapeutics, particularly GLP-1 drugs used to treat obesity and diabetes. Global demand for these treatments has surged, and pharmaceutical companies are racing to secure manufacturing capacity.

Samsung Biologics, which has built its business around antibody-based biologics, sees the deal as a way to become a multi-modality CDMO capable of serving clients across a broader range of therapeutic areas. PolyPeptide brings more than 70 years of peptide manufacturing heritage and has produced over 1,000 therapeutic peptides to date.

"This acquisition reinforces our long-term growth strategy by not only broadening our service portfolio with modality expansion into peptides including GLP-1, but by also boosting our geographic reach and proximity further within the US, Europe, and India."

— John Rim, Chairman and CEO, Samsung Biologics

A Global Manufacturing Footprint

PolyPeptide operates an integrated development-to-commercial model with manufacturing sites in Sweden, Belgium, France, the United States, and India, along with a corporate office in Switzerland and an Innovation Center in Strasbourg. This gives Samsung Biologics a significant geographic expansion from its current base in Incheon, South Korea, and Rockville, Maryland.

Samsung Biologics currently operates with a total manufacturing capacity of 845,000 litres across its Korean and US facilities. The company has secured land for a third Bio Campus to support future capacity expansion for next-generation therapies.

Deal Mechanics

PolyPeptide's board, acting through its independent members, unanimously recommended that shareholders accept the offer. The company's largest individual shareholder, Draupnir Holding, which owns about 55.65% of outstanding shares, has provided an irrevocable commitment to tender all of its shares. Draupnir's parent entity is the Cryosphere Foundation, linked to Swedish billionaire Frederik Paulsen.

The offer requires acceptance from holders of at least two-thirds of all shares on a fully diluted basis. Once completed, Samsung Biologics intends to pursue a squeeze-out of remaining minority shares and delist PolyPeptide from the SIX Swiss Exchange.

J.P. Morgan is acting as exclusive financial advisor to Samsung Biologics, with O'Melveny & Myers and Schellenberg Wittmer providing legal counsel.

What It Means for Indian Manufacturing

PolyPeptide's India operations will become part of Samsung Biologics' global network, potentially positioning the facility for expanded capacity as GLP-1 demand grows. For India's pharmaceutical manufacturing sector, the deal signals continued foreign investment in the country's drug production capabilities, particularly in high-value biologics and peptide synthesis.

The acquisition also reflects a broader industry trend where CDMOs are expanding into peptide manufacturing to capture the enormous commercial opportunity presented by weight-loss and diabetes drugs, which analysts expect to become one of the largest pharmaceutical categories in history.
